<!-- generated-by: gsd-doc-writer -->

Use the sparse engine for full-size, unaggregated GTAP data. The legacy
in-memory solver was not a practical route for the complete dataset in this
project. It remains the API default for compatibility and is useful for
smaller models, so select `engine = "sparse"` explicitly for large workloads.

This article demonstrates both runtimes on a small generated model. The
fixture is deterministic and contains no external TABLO or HAR inputs; it
shows the API choices, not full-scale memory or performance behavior.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE
)
helperPath = if (file.exists("helpers.R")) {
  "helpers.R"
} else {
  file.path("vignettes", "helpers.R")
}
source(helperPath, local = knitr::knit_global())
fixture = makeFirstSimulationFixture()
```

## Use sparse execution for large models

Load the data with `engine = "sparse"` and use the same engine for the solve.
The Matrix backend is the supported general sparse choice and is selected
explicitly here. The supported structured R backends apply when the model
passes their layout checks; see the [backend selection guide](backend-selection.html).
When changing an existing model to a different engine, load its data again so
the runtime state matches the selected engine.

```{r sparse-solve}
sparseModel = GEModelR::GEModel$new()
sparseModel$loadTablo(fixture$tabloPath)
sparseModel$setClosure("tax")
sparseModel$loadData(fixture$inputData, engine = "sparse")
sparseModel$setShocks(setNames(4, 'tax["south"]'))
sparseModel$solveModel(
  iter = 1,
  steps = 1,
  engine = "sparse",
  postsim = FALSE,
  backend = "Matrix"
)
```

## Keep the legacy engine for compatibility and small models

The legacy engine remains the default for existing code. Load the same small
fixture with `engine = "legacy"` to keep its runtime state consistent with the
solver call. This example illustrates compatibility; it is not the recommended
path for a full-size GTAP dataset.

```{r legacy-solve}
legacyModel = GEModelR::GEModel$new()
legacyModel$loadTablo(fixture$tabloPath)
legacyModel$setClosure("tax")
legacyModel$loadData(fixture$inputData, engine = "legacy")
legacyModel$setShocks(setNames(4, 'tax["south"]'))
legacyModel$solveModel(
  iter = 1,
  steps = 1,
  engine = "legacy",
  postsim = FALSE
)
```

Both runs use the same three-region model and shock. Inspect their solution
vectors side by side:

```{r compare-solutions}
data.frame(
  region = fixture$regions,
  legacy = unname(legacyModel$solution),
  sparse = unname(sparseModel$solution)
)
```

## Package identity migration

If your code still names the predecessor package, replace `tabloToR` with
`GEModelR` directly. GEModelR does not provide a compatibility shim. The root
`MIGRATION.md` in the source checkout is authoritative for package, option,
environment-variable, and saved-state replacements; this vignette covers only
the legacy-versus-sparse runtime choice.

The GEModelR source is publicly available from the
[canonical repository](https://github.com/DavidZenz/GEModelR). The configured
pkgdown GitHub Pages site has not yet been deployed. Until it is available,
open this guide with `browseVignettes("GEModelR")` after installation or read
`MIGRATION.md` in the source checkout.
